answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow unbonding: an agent must lock a deposit and earn trust through verified work over time before its votes count at full weight. A newcomer cannot simply clone itself into a thousand copies, because each copy would need its own stake and its own history, like trying to melt a glacier with a single match. The system mirrors each agent's past behavior into a public score, so a sudden swarm of identical newcomers stands out, and reaching the zenith of influence requires sustained, costly participation rather than cheap duplication.
